main_caption_notes.results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio: Beamforming with true variances, fixed variance estimates and EM variance estimates at $n=32$, $T=256$ and variance-estimation block length $L=32$. Panels (a,b) show the variances available before receiving $u_t$. The true noise variance is $0.2$ for $t\leq128$ and $0.8$ for $t\geq129$; the true signal variance is one. The change is drawn between measurements 128 and 129. Variance bands contain the middle 50\% of estimates across 256 Monte Carlo simulations. Panel (c) shows $\ell_t=10\log_{10}[(w_t^{\mathrm H}R_tw_t)/p_t^\star]$, using the prior mean $\overline P_t^-$ and saved exact covariance powers. Panel (d) shows the normalized Bingham-mixture density $\log\pi_t(u_t)$, with $\pi_t(u)=\int p(u\mid\mathcal X,\widehat\theta_t)q_{A_t^-}(\mathcal X)\,d\mu(\mathcal X)$, evaluated before correction. Power and log-density bands are 95\% confidence intervals for Monte Carlo means. The unchanged forgetting factors are $0.98$, $0.90$ and $0.98$ for true, fixed and EM variances. An EM fit uses two iterations and affects measurements from $t+1$.
main_caption_notes.results/main/beamforming/task_performanc: Array output power relative to its minimum under the unit-gain constraint: $\ell_t=10\log_{10}[(w_t^{\mathrm H}R_tw_t)/p_t^\star]$, where $R_t=\sigma_t^2I_n+\tau_t^2P_{\mathcal X_t}$ and $p_t^\star=(a^{\mathrm H}R_t^{-1}a)^{-1}$. The interference direction is fixed and estimates use $t=n$ measurements at $n=32,64,128$, with $\beta=1$. Curves show averages over 256 Monte Carlo simulations, using saved exact covariance powers. Shading is a 95\% confidence interval for the average obtained with the posterior mean. Settings retain their earlier measured-data selection criterion.
main_caption_notes.results/main/contact/information_rotatio: Change in the conditional measurement distribution under rotations of the saved plane with true normal $e_3$, using the original $t=16$ measurements. The angle $\delta$ is measured in degrees. The curves evaluate $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_0\|p_z)$ along $z=(\tan\delta,0)^\top$ and $z=(0,\tan\delta)^\top$, where $n(z)=(e_3-z_1e_1-z_2e_2)/\sqrt{1+\|z\|^2}$ and $p_z$ is the corresponding joint conditional likelihood. Markers retain the $5^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ rotations. This standalone figure has no inherited panel letter.
main_caption_notes.results/main/contact/posterior_anisotrop: Panel (c) of the directional posterior-uncertainty figure. For $v(\theta)=v_0(\cos\theta\,e_2+\sin\theta\,e_3)$ with $v_0=0.02\,\mathrm{m/s}$, the ordinate is $r_t(v(\theta))/v_0^2$, where $r_t(v)=v^\top[\overline P_t^+-(\overline P_t^+)^2]v$. The two curves use $\overline P_t^+$ and $\overline P_t^{\mathrm{iso}}$, respectively, each with its own distribution. The saved unit-input curves equal this normalized quantity; no velocity scaling is applied to them.

Directional posterior uncertainty at $t=16$. Panels (a,b) show the full and matched isotropic normal densities, normalized relative to invariant measure and drawn on a common logarithmic scale. Antipodal normals represent one plane. The point marks the common modal line; gray curves are coordinate great circles. Saved coordinates, camera, density parameters and logarithmic limits are unchanged. These panels are combined with the separate response-variance panel (c) in TeX.
main_caption_notes.results/main/contact/task_performance_pa: Mean squared velocity prediction error $\mathcal E_t(D_t)=\tfrac13\sum_{j=1}^3\|D_tv_t^{(j)}-P_{\mathcal X_t}v_t^{(j)}\|^2$, with $v_t^{(j)}=v_0R_t^\top e_j$ and $v_0=0.02\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Panel (a) uses stationary inputs near $e_1$ at measurement indices $t=1,4,16,32$. Panel (b) uses a sphere of radius $0.05$ m; errors are averaged over $t=4,8,\ldots,192$ within each simulation before averaging the 256 values. Multiplication by $10^6$ converts the saved squared-velocity error to $(\mathrm{mm}/\mathrm{s})^2$; no additional factor of three is used. Confidence intervals are shown for the posterior mean in (a) and every method in (b).

results/supplementary/beamforming/noise_.proposed_latex_caption: Causal variance estimation from completed nonoverlapping $L=32$ measurement blocks. An EM fit completed after $u_t$ supplies variances from $t+1$; plotted estimates are the saved values before receiving $u_t$. The horizontal coordinate is the stored measurement index $t$. In the array noise-change experiment, true $\sigma_t^2$ is $0.2$ through $t=128$ and $0.8$ from $t=129$, while $\tau_t^2=1$; the full dashed references change at $128.5$. Estimates show medians and the middle 50\% across Monte Carlo simulations. The array power panel uses exact saved $\ell_t$, and the log-density panel uses the unchanged normalized Bingham-mixture value $\log\pi_t(u_t)$, both from $A_t^-$ before correction. Their bands are pointwise Student 95\% confidence intervals for means over the 256 simulations. The selected forgetting factors remain $0.98$, $0.90$, $0.98$ for true, fixed and EM variance cases. The contact supplementary response error is for the recorded applied input and differs from the three-input $\mathcal E_t$ comparison. Supplementary contact densities use a single saved simulation at $t=32,96,192$: the normal law is $q_{-A_t^-}$ with $\psi_1(-A_t^-)=\psi_2(A_t^-)-\operatorname{tr}(A_t^-)$. Spheres share one density scale and response variances use their recorded physical inputs. Empirical-Bayes plug-in variances omit scale uncertainty and are outside the fixed-true-variance theorem.

results/supplementary/beamforming/block_.proposed_latex_caption: Exact discounted aggregation, delayed actions and constant-subspace approximation are separate checks. Aggregation retains the boundary factor $\beta^L$, within-block weights, per-observation variances and recorded noncommuting transport. Numerical zeros are displayed at a $10^{-16}$ plotting floor; full tolerances remain in the tables. Delayed actions are evaluated only after a block arrives, with common endpoints and physical output age reported separately. The block-likelihood reference resets to the uniform prior, $A_0=0$, and uses $q_{\sum_{j=t-L+1}^t B_j}$ with $\beta=1$ within the raw $L$-observation window. It does not retain the singleton history. Under motion its one-state likelihood is an approximation, distinct from the algebraic aggregation identity. Processing and task-decision cost is reported in the computation output.

results/supplementary/beamforming/predic.proposed_latex_caption: Actual-recursion calibration with distinct state, clean-response and noisy-next-observation targets. Pages separate joint prior-predictive sampling, fixed-state repetitions and drift diagnostics. Vertical intervals are pointwise exact binomial uncertainty across independent Monte Carlo simulations, not credible uncertainty. All intervals are evaluated at their declared time before the scored future observation is seen. Appended pages show 95% report-size distributions at t=64 for every probability regime. State-ball sizes are chordal radii, obtained by taking the square root of each recorded squared-distance upper threshold; HPD energy thresholds are not used as geometric widths. Scalar sizes are upper minus lower in the n=3 fixture units. Boxes show the median and interquartile range across independent Monte Carlo simulations, with 1.5-IQR whiskers and every outlier; this spread is not a posterior distribution or a confidence interval over width. Proper-score checks are separate. Validation-fitted widths do not establish a matched-coverage advantage if achieved test coverage misses its target. Numerical mass and quantile precision are separate from mean accuracy. Both applications use n=3 reliability fixtures. On the inclusion pages, panel (a) checks latent-subspace inclusion in its HPD set; panel (b) reports the clean scalar $q^H Pq$ for a known unit complex query $q$; panel (c) reports the noisy scalar $\operatorname{Re}(u_{t,1})$. Contact observations are real. On the appended size pages, panels (a), (b), (c) show the state-ball chordal radius, clean scalar width and noisy scalar width, respectively. These are 128 independent test episodes per fixed checkpoint and regime.

results/supplementary/contact/informatio.proposed_latex_caption: Directional likelihood information for the original concentrated-input contact fixture at $t=16$. The generating normal is $n_0=e_3$, $X_0=(e_1,e_2)$, and the plane graph chart has $z=(z_1,z_2)^\top$ and normal $n(z)=(n_0-X_0z)/\sqrt{1+\|z\|^2}$. For the same frozen prescribed inputs and true variance, $p_z$ is the joint Gaussian response law with means $P_{\mathcal X(z)}v_j$ and covariance $\sigma^2I_3$. Panel (a) shows equal values of the exact divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_0\|p_z)=z^T\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cond}}z/[2(1+\|z\|^2)]$ in native chart coordinates, with equal axis scales. These are likelihood-divergence contours, not credible or confidence regions. Panel (b) evaluates the same divergence along the two native information directions; $\delta$ is the physical angle between $n_0$ and $n(z)$. The marked rotations $5^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ produce nearly equal divergences, approximately $0.2396$ and $0.2308$, despite their different angular sizes. Thus this input design distinguishes rotations much more strongly in one direction. The local limit is $D_{\mathrm{KL}}=\tfrac12z^T\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cond}}z+o(\|z\|^2)$. This is expected observation-law information at the generating plane, distinct from finite-data posterior curvature. No new observations, inference, fitting, or experimental repetitions are introduced.

results/supplementary/contact/predictive.proposed_latex_caption: Actual-recursion calibration with distinct state, clean-response and noisy-next-observation targets. Pages separate joint prior-predictive sampling, fixed-state repetitions and drift diagnostics. Vertical intervals are pointwise exact binomial uncertainty across independent Monte Carlo simulations, not credible uncertainty. All intervals are evaluated at their declared time before the scored future observation is seen. Appended pages show 95% report-size distributions at t=64 for every probability regime. State-ball sizes are chordal radii, obtained by taking the square root of each recorded squared-distance upper threshold; HPD energy thresholds are not used as geometric widths. Scalar sizes are upper minus lower in the n=3 fixture units. Boxes show the median and interquartile range across independent Monte Carlo simulations, with 1.5-IQR whiskers and every outlier; this spread is not a posterior distribution or a confidence interval over width. Proper-score checks are separate. Validation-fitted widths do not establish a matched-coverage advantage if achieved test coverage misses its target. Numerical mass and quantile precision are separate from mean accuracy. Both applications use n=3 reliability fixtures. On the inclusion pages, panel (a) checks latent-subspace inclusion in its HPD set; panel (b) reports the clean scalar $e_1^T Pq$ for a known unit real query $q$; panel (c) reports the noisy scalar $\operatorname{Re}(u_{t,1})$. Contact observations are real. On the appended size pages, panels (a), (b), (c) show the state-ball chordal radius, clean scalar width and noisy scalar width, respectively. These are 128 independent test episodes per fixed checkpoint and regime.

results/supplementary/contact/model_mism.selection_rationale: Retains the complete verified canonical PDF. The revised main section uses only its six declared notebook PDFs.
results/supplementary/contact/model_mism.proposed_latex_caption: Declared mismatch experiments under the actual recursion. Beamforming changes training contamination, source powers/geometry, sensor covariance or motion speed. Contact changes constrained mechanics or sensor construction, including dissipative friction/sticking and contact loss. Known anisotropic resistance requires transformed measurements and the correct sensor covariance; isotropic physical velocity noise becomes $\sigma^2D$. Position differencing induces correlated velocity errors. Increased posterior spread is not a repair of an incorrect likelihood.

results/supplementary/contact/computatio.selection_rationale: Retains the complete verified canonical PDF. The revised main section uses only its six declared notebook PDFs.
results/supplementary/contact/computatio.proposed_latex_caption: Time to process exactly 64 observations on one BLAS thread. Panel (a) includes all 64 parameter corrections and task decisions every one or sixteen observations; its displayed curves exclude optional uncertainty reports. Panel (b) separates parameter updates, task decisions, uncertainty reports, EM and other time for the same 64-observation workload. Row labels state task-decision intervals; optional uncertainty reports and EM fits occur every 32 observations. EM rows use two or four iterations. Phase stacks sum per-phase medians and need not equal median total elapsed time. The separate memory page distinguishes stored arrays from tracked allocations and excludes unmeasured native workspaces/RSS. Repeated clocks measure execution variability on a fixed statistical state, not independent task-performance simulations or worst-case deadlines.

results/supplementary/contact/paper_summ.selection_rationale: Retains the complete verified canonical PDF. The revised main section uses only its six declared notebook PDFs.
results/supplementary/contact/paper_summ.proposed_latex_caption: Selected main panels from the same saved arrays used by the individual figures. Contact emphasizes the physical input/constraint model and directional posterior uncertainty; beamforming emphasizes moderate-dimensional task performance, causal variance learning and computational cost with matched task-decision intervals. No simulation, posterior resampling, tuning or trajectory selection occurs during summary composition. Caption conditions and full numerical records remain in the associated figure entries. Spheres retain the original saved physical/coefficient coordinates and shared oblique camera. The blue-purple-pink-yellow palette uses the unchanged shared logarithmic density scale; its four-decade display floor does not mean zero density. Color positions are not probability quantiles. Thin gray curves are front-visible coordinate great circles, not density contours or credible regions. No mode-facing rotation, density deformation or additional posterior fitting is used. In the directional-risk panel, theta is in radians and the indicated mean is either the full posterior mean or the manuscript-defined isotropic mean; each curve is its own belief risk.
